definitions.explanation: A shop that sells bread and baked goods, or a person who runs such a shop.

examples.english: I bought bread at the bakery in the morning.

examples.japanese: ⟦{駅前|えきまえ}→駅前：09593_ekimae⟧⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{新|あたら}しい→新しい：00506_atarashii⟧パン{屋|や}⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できた→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: A new bakery opened in front of the station.

examples.japanese: ⟦この→この：00962_kono⟧パン{屋|や}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{朝|あさ}→朝：02277_asa⟧⟦{早|はや}く→早く：02935_hayaku⟧⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦{焼|や}きたて→焼きたて：16735_yakitate⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{出|だ}す→出す：01087_dasu⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧で、⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{行列|ぎょうれつ}→行列：09699_gyouretsu⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧⟦できている→できる：00557_dekiru⟧。
examples.english: This bakery serves freshly baked bread from early morning, so there is always a line.

notes:
パン{屋|や} is a shop that sells bread and baked goods, or the person who runs such a shop. Japanese bakeries typically display a wide selection of individual rolls and pastries on trays, and customers pick items with tongs before paying at the register.

PATTERN: Follows the common product + ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ (shop/seller) pattern: ⟦{花屋|はなや}→花屋：03136_hanaya⟧ (florist), ⟦{本屋|ほんや}→本屋：03034_honya⟧ (bookshop), ⟦{魚屋|さかなや}→魚屋：14642_sakanaya⟧ (fish shop). The ⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧ suffix can refer to either the shop or the person who runs it.

COMMON COLLOCATIONS:
- パン{屋|や}⟦に→に：00314_ni⟧⟦{行|い}く→行く：00119_iku⟧: to go to the bakery
- パン{屋|や}⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦{買|か}う→買う：00489_kau⟧: to buy at the bakery
- パン{屋|や}⟦を→を：00422_wo⟧⟦{開|ひら}く→開く：01979_hiraku⟧: to open a bakery
- ⟦{町|まち}→町：00613_machi⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧パン{屋|や}: the neighborhood bakery

SIMILAR WORDS:
- ベーカリー: bakery (from English, often used for upscale or chain shops)
- ⟦{菓子|かし}→菓子：00191_kashi⟧⟦{屋|や}→〜屋：03096_ya⟧: confectionery shop (sweets and cakes, not bread)
- ⟦パン→パン：00553_pan⟧⟦{工房|こうぼう}→工房：12418_koubou⟧: bread workshop/artisan bakery
